A.explanation: Acceleration is rate of change of velocity so its unit is $\text{m s}^{-2}$, not $\text{m s}^{-1}$ which is the unit of velocity.

B.explanation: Electric current is charge per unit time and is measured in ampere, so $\text{A}$ alone is correct and $\text{A s}^{-1}$ is wrong.

C.explanation: Potential difference is energy transferred per unit charge, $V = W/Q$, so $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$ and $8.0 \text{ J C}^{-1}$ is correct.

D.explanation: Kinetic energy is measured in joule where $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$, so $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is wrong.

hints: Look at the unit attached to each quantity: acceleration in A, current in B, potential difference in C, and energy in D.
Recall the defining equations $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$, $I = Q/t$, $V = W/Q$ and $W = F \times d$ to work out what each base combination should be.
Check which $\text{J C}^{-1}$ means joule per coulomb and compare it with energy per charge, then eliminate the options where an extra $\text{s}^{-1}$ or $\text{m}^{-1}$ has been added.
walkthrough: Identify the four pairs: A links acceleration to $\text{m s}^{-1}$, B links current to $\text{A s}^{-1}$, C links potential difference to $\text{J C}^{-1}$, D links kinetic energy to $\text{N m}^{-1}$.

State the correct units from definitions: acceleration is $\text{m s}^{-2}$, current is $\text{A}$, potential difference is energy per charge in $\text{J C}^{-1}$ or volt, and energy is $\text{N m}$ or joule.
Compare each option: A uses the unit of velocity, B divides current by time again, and D divides force times distance by length again, so all three are inconsistent.
For C, use $V = W/Q$ where $W$ is in $\text{J}$ and $Q$ is in $\text{C}$, giving $V$ in $\text{J C}^{-1}$, so $8.0 \text{ J C}^{-1}$ is a valid potential difference. This is option C.
